sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 7.7% a year from FY2018 to FY2025, reaching $25.8 billion [F1][F8][F145].
The path was a step change rather than a smooth climb: revenue jumped 22.3% in FY2022 to $23.0 billion, then fell 5.2% in FY2024 before recovering 9.8% in FY2025 [F5][F7][F8][D131][D201][D236].
The FY2024 decline came from lower storm cost recovery revenues of about $1,090 million and lower fuel cost recovery revenues of about $526 million [P34][P35].
The FY2025 rebound reflected higher storm cost recovery revenues of about $1,091 million and a $217 million increase in storm protection plan cost recovery [P18][P21].
Operating income grew faster than revenue at a 9.9% CAGR, but net income grew only 0.4% and diluted EPS fell 0.7% a year [F145][F146][F147][F149].
FPL supplied 70.5% of FY2025 revenue at $18.2 billion [S6][D271].
FPL contributed 5.5pp of the 9.8% FY2025 revenue growth, and its revenue rose 7.7% [D236][D272][D273].
FPL's revenue increase was driven by higher storm cost recovery, retail base and storm protection plan cost recovery revenues, partly offset by lower fuel cost recovery [P21].
NEER's FY2025 results rose on higher earnings from new investments, with 1,604 MW of wind, 2,859 MW of solar and 1,799 MW of battery storage added [P26].
Operating income grew 10.7% against 9.8% revenue growth in FY2025, but operating costs grew 10.0%, so the incremental margin was only 34.8% [D236][D237][D249][D256].
The FY2025 operating margin of 32.1% sits above the 30.3% window median but well below the 41.3% FY2023 high and far above the 15.5% FY2021 low [F24][D298][D299][D300].
The FY2023 margin spike of 23.5pp came with operating income up 150.8%, and the FY2024 reversal of 9.5pp followed a 26.9% operating income decline [D177][D167][D212][D202].
FY2025 D&A rose $951 million, mainly on about $1,090 million of higher storm cost amortization, and D&A reached 25.5% of revenue [X32][D224][P16].
Net margin fell 3.1pp to 26.5% as Corporate and Other results dropped $1,256 million, largely on about $1,002 million of unfavorable non-qualifying hedge activity [F40][D248][P8].
The effective tax rate swung to -17.7% from 5.6%, reflecting clean energy tax credits that rose about $585 million [D226][D191][P11].
Operating cash flow of $12.5 billion was 1.83x net income in FY2025, in line with the 1.55x to 2.73x range across the window [F64][F32][D227][D157][D52].
Operating cash flow fell 5.8% in FY2025 while investing outflow reached $23.9 billion, so free cash flow stayed deeply negative [D241][F72].
The swing from net over-recovery to net under-recovery of cost recovery clauses cut FPL's operating cash flow by about $89 million [P19].
Stock-based compensation is immaterial to cash, at 1.5% of operating cash flow in FY2025 [D228].
Total debt rose 15.7% to $95.0 billion in FY2025 while cash and investments were $2.8 billion, leaving net debt of $92.2 billion [D230][D229][D231][D253].
Net cash has fallen every year since FY2018, from -$34.3 billion to -$92.2 billion, and net cash as a share of revenue ranks at the 0th percentile against four utilities peers [D9][D231][D232][D314].
The current ratio of 0.60x is the window high but still below 1.0x, with working capital of -$9.2 billion [F128][D305][F120].
Dividends of $4.7 billion were paid in FY2025, and the diluted share count rose 0.6% [X82][D251].
The current ratio has stayed below 1.0x in every year of the window, from 0.36x in FY2018 to 0.60x in FY2025, so the FY2025 reading is structural rather than new [F121][F128][R1].
Net cash has fallen for seven straight years, from -$34.3 billion in FY2018 to -$92.2 billion in FY2025, as long-term debt compounded at 18.8% against 6.9% equity growth [D9][D231][F156][F157][R2].
The FY2024 revenue decline of 5.2% was a pass-through effect of lower storm and fuel cost recovery revenues, not a demand loss [F7][D201][P34][R3].
The FY2025 tax-rate swing to -17.7% reflects clean energy credits and NEER's pretax mix, so it is a recurring feature of the tax profile rather than a one-off error [D226][P11][R4].
Watch the operating margin against the 30.3% window median; a print below it would reverse the FY2025 stabilisation at 32.1% [D300][F24].
Watch net debt against the FY2025 level of $92.2 billion; further deepening would extend the seven-year trend [D231].
Watch operating cash flow against the FY2025 $12.5 billion; a second consecutive decline would confirm the FY2025 5.8% drop as a trend [F64][D241].
